wenn die app im hintergrund ist ist aktuell eine fest eingestellte genauigkeit konfiguriert für die location updates. Ich möchte dem Nutzer die möglichkeit geben auch diese hintergrund-genauigkeit einzustellen, sprich die "significant location change" api so zu konfigurieren dass weniger bewegung benötigt wird um ein location update auszulösen. Wie könnte ich das am besten machen, ich möchte in den erweiterten Einstellungen in der passenden Sektion diese Einstellungen dem nutzer zur verfügng stellen und die aktuellne defaults übernehmen

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-25 11:37:15Z)**_

Klar, ich würde den Plan so ergänzen:

```md
## Zusatz: Automatische Rückkehr zum Standard-Modus
- Neue Settings:
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesEnabled`, Default `false`
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesDuration`, Default `4h`
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesExpiresAt`, optionales Ablaufdatum
- In den erweiterten Einstellungen:
  - Toggle “Häufigere Hintergrund-Updates”
  - Picker “Automatisch deaktivieren nach” mit:
    - `1 Stunde`
    - `4 Stunden` (Default)
    - `12 Stunden`
    - `24 Stunden`
    - `Unendlich`
- Aktivierungslogik:
  - Wenn der Nutzer den Toggle einschaltet, wird `expiresAt = now + selectedDuration` gesetzt.
  - Bei “Unendlich” bleibt `expiresAt = nil`.
  - Wenn der Nutzer die Dauer während aktivem Modus ändert, wird die Ablaufzeit ab diesem Moment neu berechnet.
- Ablaufverhalten:
  - Sobald `expiresAt` erreicht ist, setzt die App `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesEnabled = false`.
  - Danach wird automatisch wieder der bisherige Default-Pfad genutzt: `startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges()`.
  - Das Ablaufdatum wird gelöscht.
- Robustheit:
  - Ablaufprüfung nicht nur über einen Timer, sondern auch bei App-Start, Foreground/Background-Wechsel, Settings-Änderungen und jedem Location-Update ausführen.
  - Damit funktioniert die Rückkehr auch dann korrekt, wenn iOS die App nicht exakt zur Ablaufzeit weckt.
```

Damit bleibt das bisherige Verhalten weiterhin der sichere Default, und der neue Modus ist bewusst als temporärer “mehr Updates jetzt”-Modus gestaltet.

Hier ist der aktualisierte komplette Plan:

<proposed_plan>
# Einstellbare Hintergrund-Standortupdates

## Summary
- Das aktuelle `significant location change`-Verhalten bleibt unverändert der Default.
- Der neue Modus wird explizit per Toggle aktiviert und nutzt häufigere Background-Updates über normale Location-Updates mit Distanzfilter.
- Der neue Modus ist standardmäßig zeitlich begrenzt: Default `4 Stunden`, danach Rückkehr zum significant-change-Modus.

## Key Changes
- Settings ergänzen:
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesEnabled`, Default `false`
  - `backgroundLocationDistanceFilterMeters`, Default `100`
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesDuration`, Default `4h`
  - `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesExpiresAt`, optionales Ablaufdatum
- UI in den erweiterten Einstellungen:
  - Toggle “Häufigere Hintergrund-Updates”
  - Bei aktivem Toggle Picker “Bewegungsschwelle”: `100 m`, `50 m`, `25 m`
  - Bei aktivem Toggle Picker “Automatisch deaktivieren nach”: `1 Stunde`, `4 Stunden`, `12 Stunden`, `24 Stunden`, `Unendlich`
  - Erklärung: aus = aktueller Energiesparmodus, an = häufigere Updates mit höherem Akkuverbrauch.
- Aktivierungslogik:
  - Beim Einschalten wird `expiresAt` anhand der gewählten Dauer gesetzt.
  - Bei `Unendlich` bleibt `expiresAt = nil`.
  - Wenn die Dauer während aktivem Modus geändert wird, wird `expiresAt` ab diesem Zeitpunkt neu berechnet.
  - Beim manuellen Ausschalten wird `expiresAt` gelöscht.
- `LocationManager`:
  - Toggle aus oder abgelaufen: heutiger Pfad mit `startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges()`.
  - Toggle an und nicht abgelaufen: `startUpdatingLocation()` im Hintergrund mit `allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true`, gewähltem `distanceFilter` und passender `desiredAccuracy`.
  - Ablaufprüfung bei App-Start, Foreground/Background-Wechsel, Settings-Änderungen und jedem Location-Update.
- Status-/Hinweistexte:
  - Default: “Energiesparmodus / signifikante Bewegungen”
  - Neuer Modus: “Häufigere Hintergrund-Updates / X m”, optional mit Restlaufzeit.
- Settings.bundle, Localizable-Strings und DeviceKey-Settings-Snapshot um die neuen Werte erweitern.

## Test Plan
- Settings-Tests:
  - neue Defaults: Toggle `false`, Distanz `100`, Dauer `4h`, Ablaufdatum leer
  - Settings.bundle-Defaults stimmen mit Runtime-Defaults überein
  - neue Lokalisierungskeys existieren in allen Locales
- Location-Logik:
  - Toggle aus nutzt significant-change.
  - Toggle an nutzt standard background updates mit korrektem Distanzfilter.
  - Abgelaufener Modus deaktiviert sich selbst und kehrt zu significant-change zurück.
  - `Unendlich` läuft nicht automatisch ab.
- Verifikation: `./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh`

## Assumptions
- Die significant-change-API selbst wird nicht feiner konfiguriert, weil iOS `desiredAccuracy` und `distanceFilter` dafür ignoriert.
- Die automatische Deaktivierung erfolgt zuverlässig beim nächsten App-Wake/Location-Event/Lifecycle-Event, aber iOS muss die App nicht exakt zur Ablaufzeit wecken.
</proposed_plan>

def q(value)
  JSON.generate(value)

def entry(key, translations, comment = nil)
  lines = []
  lines << "    #{q(key)} : {"
  lines << "      \"comment\" : #{q(comment)}," if comment
  lines << "      \"localizations\" : {"
  translations.each_with_index do |(locale, value), index|

    lines << "          \"stringUnit\" : {"
    lines << "            \"state\" : \"translated\","
    lines << "            \"value\" : #{q(value)}"
    lines << "          }"
    lines << "        }#{index == translations.length - 1 ? '' : ','}"
  end
  lines << "      }"
  lines << "    }"
  lines.join("\n")
end

  next if content.include?("    #{q(key)} : {")
  ordered = locales.map { |locale| [locale, translations.fetch(locale)] }
  blocks << entry(key, ordered, comment)

version 3.1.7
- Fixed offline `UpdateLocation` delivery so new updates are queued behind already pending outbox items and retried in FIFO order without replacing the original event payload metadata.
- Added a location-status statistic for queued location updates that still need to be sent.
- Added Advanced Options controls for the unsent location-update queue retention and capacity, keeping the default at 24 hours / 500 updates while allowing longer retention, unlimited retention, and higher caps.
- Added a confirmation step when changing the Miataru server URL while location updates are queued, allowing the user to send queued updates to the new server or discard them.
- Improved queued-update draining so active tracking schedules near-term FIFO flushes, full batches continue automatically, and the location-status view can manually flush all currently deliverable queued updates.
- Hardened queued-update server URL retargeting so already queued items are consistently rewritten to the chosen new server and in-flight old-URL sends cannot remove retargeted queue records.
- Added regression coverage for queued-update ordering, configurable outbox policy changes, server URL retargeting, full queue flushes, and settings/localization parity.
- Added visible loading feedback when opening a device's location history on iPhone and iPad, including the selected device name/ID while history data is being preloaded.
- Prevented the history map from briefly showing the "no location history" fallback before cached or freshly loaded history entries have been applied.
- Improved history-load error handling so invalid configuration, server/response failures, encoding/decoding failures, network failures, and unknown failures produce readable user-facing messages.
- Added full localization coverage for the new history loading text across all supported app languages.
- Made common error overlays wrap long messages more reliably and kept history preload errors visible longer.
- Kept manual pan/zoom interaction on the device history map authoritative during live history refreshes, so newly recorded positions no longer force the map to refit after the user has adjusted the camera.

version 3.1.5
- Refactored the iOS settings flow: centralized runtime defaults and one-time existing-install migrations, shortened the root settings screen, added a dedicated `Advanced Options` page, and moved ACL/status content to the intended destinations.
- Synchronized settings defaults, labels, picker options, and explanatory copy across `Localizable.xcstrings` and all supported `Settings.bundle` locales.
- Added regression coverage for settings defaults, settings localization completeness, `Settings.bundle` parity, and the advanced-options navigation path, with updated test documentation.
- Fixed device-slogan editing so normal spaces remain typeable while final save cleansing still trims outer whitespace and removes control characters.
- Changed the device-slogan fetch strategy: `Add Device` and `Edit Device` use `getDeviceSlogan`, unknown devices in the iPhone/iPad device lists only fetch missing slogans individually after the normal `getLocation` refresh, and all other slogan reads continue to rely on `getLocation`.

version 3.1.4
- Extended `MiataruClientSwift` with typed support for `getAllowedDeviceList` (`MiataruGetAllowedDeviceList` request and `MiataruAllowedDeviceList` response model).
- Added `MiataruAPIClient.getAllowedDeviceList(...)` for authenticated owner reads against `v1/getAllowedDeviceList`.
- Updated `MiataruClientSwift` README with usage documentation and example code for `getAllowedDeviceList`.
- Fixed intermittent Devices-list refresh flicker where rows briefly dropped all supplemental information and showed only the device name during active polling.
- Coalesced overlapping device-list refresh requests into a single in-flight fetch and now apply refreshed device-location cache data as one consolidated snapshot instead of publishing per-device partial states.
- Kept the last successful device-location cache visible on transient refresh failures, avoiding the short-lived blank/half-empty list state during network hiccups.
- Fixed standard navigation summary countdown on iPhone and iPad so ETA/distance no longer jump from the initially correct route values to `0 km / 0 min` right after route calculation.
- Standard `device -> user` navigation now seeds live summary updates from the moment the active route is applied (including cached routes), instead of reusing potentially stale device sample timestamps.
- Added centralized device-slogan cleansing before every `setDeviceSlogan` request (remove control characters, trim outer whitespace, enforce max length 40) so invalid special/control characters are not sent to the server.
- Replaced raw server error text in slogan-save UI with a user-friendly localized fallback message ("B

# Device History Map User Camera Priority

## Problem

The device history view refreshes its history data while it is open. For the owner's own device this can happen during movement: a new location enters the shared location cache, the history view fetches fresh server history, and `viewModel.history` publishes the updated entries.

Before this change, every history publication called `updateRegion(animated: false)`. That was correct for the initial view setup, but wrong after manual map interaction: if the user had panned or zoomed the history map, the next live refresh immediately refit the camera around the visible history points.

## Change

`iPhone_DeviceHistoryMapView` now tracks whether the user has adjusted the map camera by observing non-suppressed center or zoom changes from `onMapCameraChange`.

History reloads still update the timeline, annotations, and route polyline, but automatic region fitting now goes through `updateRegionIfUserCameraAllows(animated:)`. Once the user has panned or zoomed, live history refreshes no longer override the current camera.

Programmatic camera updates keep using the existing suppression window so the initial fit, playback focus, and other explicit camera moves do not mark the map as manually adjusted.

Quick range selection resets the manual-camera flag because selecting a new range is an explicit request to refit the visible history slice.

## Verification

Built successfully with:

```sh
xcodebuild -project miataru.xcodeproj -scheme miataru -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build
```

```diff
+# Frequent Background Location Updates
+
+## Problem
+
+Miataru previously used iOS significant-change monitoring for background location tracking. That behavior is battery-friendly and remains the default, but it only wakes the app after larger movement. Some users need a temporary mode that reports background movement more often without changing the default behavior for everyone else.
+
+## Change
+
+Advanced Options now include an explicit frequent-background update toggle in the background location section. The toggle defaults to off, so existing users continue to use significant-change monitoring unless they opt in.
+
+When the mode is enabled, users can choose a background distance filter:
+
+- 100 m (default)
+- 50 m
+- 25 m
+
+Users can also choose when the mode should disable itself:
+
+- 1 hour
+- 4 hours (default)
+- 12 hours
+- 24 hours
+- Never
+
+The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.
+
+Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.
+
+## Runtime Behavior
+
+`SettingsManager` owns the new persisted settings and normalizes unsupported distance or duration values back to the shipped defaults. The DeviceKey recovery/reset snapshot now includes these settings so that identity changes do not silently reset the user's background-tracking preference.
+
+`LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.
+
+The location-status view now shows whether background tracking is using significant-change monitoring or frequent updates. If frequent updates have a finite expiration date, the status card also shows when the mode will revert.
+
+## Verification
+
+Validated with:
+
+```sh
+./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh
+./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh -only-testing:miataruTests/SettingsConfigurationTests
+git diff --check
+```
```

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-26 00:52:55Z)**_

Kurz gesagt: Der „Timeout“ ist kein iOS-Background-Task, sondern ein persistierter Ablaufzeitpunkt plus mehrere Sicherheitschecks.

Wenn der Nutzer die Option einschaltet, setzt `SettingsManager` ein `expiresAt` auf `jetzt + Dauer`, also bei Default z.B. 4 Stunden: [SettingsManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/SettingsManager.swift:79) und [SettingsConfiguration.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/SettingsConfiguration.swift:140). Ändert der Nutzer die Dauer während die Option aktiv ist, wird der Ablaufzeitpunkt neu ab „jetzt“ berechnet. Bei „Nie“ wird kein Ablaufdatum gespeichert.

Abgeschaltet wird auf zwei Arten:

1. Solange die App läuft, plant `LocationManager` einen normalen `Timer` bis `expiresAt`. Wenn der feuert, wird `frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesEnabled = false` gesetzt und der Tracking-Modus neu angewendet: [LocationManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/LocationManager.swift:501).

2. Weil iOS Apps im Hintergrund suspendieren oder beenden kann, wird zusätzlich bei vielen Einstiegspunkten geprüft: App-Start, foreground/background, Tracking-Start, Settings-Änderung, Start der Background-Updates und bei jedem Location-Callback. Wenn der Zeitpunkt überschritten ist, wird die Option deaktiviert und wieder auf Significant-Change-Monitoring gewechselt: [LocationManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/LocationManager.swift:490), [SettingsManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/SettingsManager.swift:336).

Kann es versehentlich an bleiben? Nicht dauerhaft als Einstellung. Wenn iOS die App genau zum Ablaufzeitpunkt schlafen legt, feuert der Timer nicht exakt in dieser Sekunde. Aber der Ablaufzeitpunkt ist gespeichert; sobald die App wieder läuft oder durch Location geweckt wird, wird sofort geprüft und deaktiviert. Bei einem Location-Update nach Ablauf wird sogar zuerst zurück auf Significant-Change geschaltet und dieses Update nicht mehr als normaler Frequent-Background-Update weiterverarbeitet: [LocationManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/LocationManager.swift:793).

Einzige Ausnahme ist bewusst: Wenn der Nutzer „Nie“ auswählt, gibt es keinen automatischen Ablauf.

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-26 00:56:27Z)**_

Kurz: einen **wirklich sicheren Weck-Timer nach exakt 4 Stunden gibt iOS nicht**.

Ein normaler `Timer` läuft nur, solange die App tatsächlich ausgeführt wird. Wenn iOS die App im Hintergrund suspendiert, feuert er nicht. Apple beschreibt genau dieses Modell: Hintergrund-Apps werden typischerweise suspendiert; BackgroundTasks können Apps zwar später ausführen, aber `earliestBeginDate` ist nur „nicht vor diesem Zeitpunkt“, keine Garantie für genau dann. Quellen: [Handling location updates in the background](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/handling-location-updates-in-the-background), [BGTaskRequest.earliestBeginDate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/backgroundtasks/bgtaskrequest/earliestbegindate).

Was man machen kann:

1. **So wie jetzt:** Ablaufdatum speichern und bei jedem Wake prüfen. Das ist robust gegen App-Neustart, Suspend, Kill usw. Es schaltet spätestens beim nächsten App-Lauf oder Location-Callback ab.

2. **Zusätzlich als Sicherheitsnetz:** `BGTaskScheduler` mit `earliestBeginDate = expiresAt` registrieren. Wenn iOS die App irgendwann danach weckt, kann sie die Option abschalten. Das verbessert die Chance, ist aber nicht garantiert und kann deutlich später passieren.

3. **Optional:** Beim Aktivieren/Ändern des Modus zusätzlich eine lokale Notification planen, die den Nutzer informiert: „Erhöhte Hintergrundgenauigkeit ist abgelaufen“. Aber Code wird dadurch nicht zuverlässig ausgeführt, außer der Nutzer öffnet die App.

„Kann es versehentlich an bleiben?“  
Als Einstellung dauerhaft: eher nein, weil `expiresAt` gespeichert ist und beim nächsten Lebenszeichen sofort greift. Als aktiver CoreLocation-Modus bis zum nächsten Wake: ja, theoretisch kann iOS die App schlafen legen und unser Code läuft dann nicht exakt zur Ablaufsekunde. Ein BGTask-Watchdog wäre der sinnvollste zusätzliche Schutz, aber auch der wäre nur best effort, nicht hart garantiert.

@@
 Users can also choose when the mode should disable itself:
 
 - 1 hour
 - 4 hours (default)
 - 12 hours
 - 24 hours
 - Never
 
 The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.
+
+Users can also choose how frequent background updates are delivered to the server:
+
+- Immediately (default)
+- Every 30 seconds
+- Every minute
+- Every 5 minutes
+- Every 10 minutes
+
+Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.
 
 Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.
@@
 `LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.
+
+When delayed delivery is selected, `LocationManager` passes the selected delay only for non-active app states while frequent background updates are enabled. Foreground updates and the default significant-change mode continue to use immediate delivery.
+
+`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately.
 
 The location-status view now shows whether background tracking is using significant-change monitoring or frequent updates. If frequent updates have a finite expiration date, the status card also shows when the mode will revert.

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-26 08:20:26Z)**_

Erledigt. Ich habe die zusätzliche Versandoption eingebaut:

In den erweiterten Einstellungen erscheint bei aktivierten häufigeren Hintergrund-Updates jetzt eine Auswahl „An Server senden“ mit:

- `Sofort` als Default, bisheriges Verhalten bleibt unverändert
- `Alle 30 Sekunden`
- `Alle 1 Minute`
- `Alle 5 Minuten`
- `Alle 10 Minuten`

Technisch läuft das über die bestehende persistente Outbox: verzögerte Hintergrund-Updates bekommen ein `availableAfter`-Datum. Weitere Updates innerhalb desselben Fensters teilen sich diesen Zeitpunkt und werden danach gemeinsam über den bestehenden FIFO-Flush verarbeitet. Es ist kein neues Server-Protokoll und kein einzelner Multi-Location-HTTP-Request, sondern ein bewusst verzögerter gemeinsamer Outbox-Flush.

Geändert sind u.a. [LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/Networking/LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator.swift:101), [LocationUpdateOutboxStore.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/Networking/LocationUpdateOutboxStore.swift:17), [LocationManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/LocationManager.swift:542) und die Settings-UI in [iPhone_AdvancedOptionsView.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Settings%20Views/iPhone_AdvancedOptionsView.swift:70).

Verifikation ist grün: `jq`, `plutil`, `git diff --check`, gezielte Tests und komplette Unit-Suite (`96 tests`) bestanden. Änderungen sind aktuell noch nicht committed.

@@
 - Added frequent-background delivery options so updates can keep sending immediately by default or be queued locally and flushed together after 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, or 10 minutes.
+- Added localized per-option explanations for frequent background movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and server-delivery mode choices.
 - Added localized red battery-usage warning text while frequent background updates are enabled, plus background-mode/expiry visibility in the location-status view.

**Update: `/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/documentation/frequent-background-location-updates-2026-04-26.md`**

```diff
@@
 Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.
 
+The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and delivery mode. These explanations make the battery and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.
+
 Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.
```

version 3.1.7
- Added an opt-in frequent background location-update mode in Advanced Options, keeping significant-change monitoring as the unchanged default when the user does not enable it.
- Added configurable frequent-background distance presets (100 m default, 50 m, 25 m) and auto-disable durations (1 hour, 4 hours default, 12 hours, 24 hours, never), with automatic fallback to significant-change monitoring after expiry.
- Added frequent-background delivery options so updates can keep sending immediately by default or be queued locally and flushed together after 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, or 10 minutes.
- Added localized per-option explanations for frequent background movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and server-delivery mode choices.
- Added localized red battery-usage warning text while frequent background updates are enabled, plus background-mode/expiry visibility in the location-status view.
- Preserved frequent-background update settings during DeviceKey recovery/reset flows and added regression coverage for defaults, localization parity, value normalization, expiry behavior, and default significant-change configuration.
- Incremented iOS app build number (`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`) from 1 to 2.
- Fixed offline `UpdateLocation` delivery so new updates are queued behind already pending outbox items and retried in FIFO order without replacing the original event payload metadata.
- Added a location-status statistic for queued location updates that still need to be sent.
- Added Advanced Options controls for the unsent location-update queue retention and capacity, keeping the default at 24 hours / 500 updates while allowing longer retention, unlimited retention, and higher caps.
- Added a confirmation step when changing the Miataru server URL while location updates are queued, allowing the user to send queued updates to the new server or discard them.
- Improved queued-update draining so active tracking schedules near-term FIFO flushes, full batches continue automatically, and the location-status view can manually flush all currently deliverable queued updates.
- Hardened queued-update server URL retargeting so already queued items are consistently rewritten to the chosen new server and in-flight old-URL sends cannot remove retargeted queue records.
- Added regression coverage for queued-update ordering, configurable outbox policy changes, server URL retargeting, full queue flushes, and settings/localization parity.
- Added visible loading feedback when opening a device's location history on iPhone and iPad, including the selected device name/ID while history data is being preloaded.
- Prevented the history map from briefly showing the "no location history" fallback before cached or freshly loaded history entries have been applied.
- Improved history-load error handling so invalid configuration, server/response failures, encoding/decoding failures, network failures, and unknown failures produce readable user-facing messages.
```

# Frequent Background Location Updates

## Problem

Miataru previously used iOS significant-change monitoring for background location tracking. That behavior is battery-friendly and remains the default, but it only wakes the app after larger movement. Some users need a temporary mode that reports background movement more often without changing the default behavior for everyone else.

## Change

Advanced Options now include an explicit frequent-background update toggle in the background location section. The toggle defaults to off, so existing users continue to use significant-change monitoring unless they opt in.

When the mode is enabled, users can choose a background distance filter:

- 100 m (default)
- 50 m
- 25 m

Users can also choose when the mode should disable itself:

- 1 hour
- 4 hours (default)
- 12 hours
- 24 hours
- Never

The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.

Users can also choose how frequent background updates are delivered to the server:

- Immediately (default)
- Every 30 seconds
- Every minute
- Every 5 minutes
- Every 10 minutes

Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.

The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and delivery mode. These explanations make the battery and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.

Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.

## Runtime Behavior

`SettingsManager` owns the new persisted settings and normalizes unsupported distance or duration values back to the shipped defaults. The DeviceKey recovery/reset snapshot now includes these settings so that identity changes do not silently reset the user's background-tracking preference.

`LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.

When delayed delivery is selected, `LocationManager` passes the selected delay only for non-active app states while frequent background updates are enabled. Foreground updates and the default significant-change mode continue to use immediate delivery.

`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately.

The location-status view now shows whether background tracking is using significant-change monitoring or frequent updates. If frequent updates have a finite expiration date, the status card also shows when the mode will revert.

## Verification

Validated with:

```sh
./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh
./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh -only-testing:miataruTests/SettingsConfigurationTests
git diff --check
```
```

     1	version 3.1.7
     2	- Added an opt-in frequent background location-update mode in Advanced Options, keeping significant-change monitoring as the unchanged default when the user does not enable it.
     3	- Added configurable frequent-background distance presets (100 m default, 50 m, 25 m) and auto-disable durations (1 hour, 4 hours default, 12 hours, 24 hours, never), with automatic fallback to significant-change monitoring after expiry.
     4	- Added frequent-background delivery options so updates can keep sending immediately by default or be queued locally and flushed together after 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, or 10 minutes.
     5	- Added localized per-option explanations for frequent background movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and server-delivery mode choices.
     6	- Added localized red battery-usage warning text while frequent background updates are enabled, plus background-mode/expiry visibility in the location-status view.
     7	- Preserved frequent-background update settings during DeviceKey recovery/reset flows and added regression coverage for defaults, localization parity, value normalization, expiry behavior, and default significant-change configuration.
     8	- Incremented iOS app build number (`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`) from 1 to 2.
     9	- Fixed offline `UpdateLocation` delivery so new updates are queued behind already pending outbox items and retried in FIFO order without replacing the original event payload metadata.
    10	- Added a location-status statistic for queued location updates that still need to be sent.
    11	- Added Advanced Options controls for the unsent location-update queue retention and capacity, keeping the default at 24 hours / 500 updates while allowing longer retention, unlimited retention, and higher caps.
    12	- Added a confirmation step when changing the Miataru server URL while location updates are queued, allowing the user to send queued updates to the new server or discard them.
    13	- Improved queued-update draining so active tracking schedules near-term FIFO flushes, full batches continue automatically, and the location-status view can manually flush all currently deliverable queued updates.
    14	- Hardened queued-update server URL retargeting so already queued items are consistently rewritten to the chosen new server and in-flight old-URL sends cannot remove retargeted queue records.
    15	- Added regression coverage for queued-update ordering, configurable outbox policy changes, server URL retargeting, full queue flushes, and settings/localization parity.
    16	- Added visible loading feedback when opening a device's location history on iPhone and iPad, including the selected device name/ID while history data is being preloaded.
    17	- Prevented the history map from briefly showing the "no location history" fallback before cached or freshly loaded history entries have been applied.
    18	- Improved history-load error handling so invalid configuration, server/response failures, encoding/decoding failures, network failures, and unknown failures produce readable user-facing messages.
    19	- Added full localization coverage for the new history loading text across all supported app languages.
    20	- Made common error overlays wrap long messages more reliably and kept history preload errors visible longer.
    21	- Kept manual pan/zoom interaction on the device history map authoritative during live history refreshes, so newly recorded positions no longer force the map to refit after the user has adjusted the camera.
    22	
    23	version 3.1.5
    24	- Refactored the iOS settings flow: centralized runtime defaults and one-time existing-install migrations, shortened the root settings screen, added a dedicated `Advanced Options` page, and moved ACL/status content to the intended destinations.
    25	- Synchronized settings defaults, labels, picker options, and explanatory copy across `Localizable.xcstrings` and all supported `Settings.bundle` locales.
    26	- Added regression coverage for settings defaults, settings localization completeness, `Settings.bundle` parity, and the advanced-options navigation path, with updated test documentation.
    27	- Fixed device-slogan editing so normal spaces remain typeable while final save cleansing still trims outer whitespace and removes control characters.
    28	- Changed the device-slogan fetch strategy: `Add Device` and `Edit Device` use `getDeviceSlogan`, unknown devices in the iPhone/iPad device lists only fetch missing slogans individually after the normal `getLocation` refresh, and all other slogan reads continue to rely on `getLocation`.

     1	# Frequent Background Location Updates
     2	
     3	## Problem
     4	
     5	Miataru previously used iOS significant-change monitoring for background location tracking. That behavior is battery-friendly and remains the default, but it only wakes the app after larger movement. Some users need a temporary mode that reports background movement more often without changing the default behavior for everyone else.
     6	
     7	## Change
     8	
     9	Advanced Options now include an explicit frequent-background update toggle in the background location section. The toggle defaults to off, so existing users continue to use significant-change monitoring unless they opt in.
    10	
    11	When the mode is enabled, users can choose a background distance filter:
    12	
    13	- 100 m (default)
    14	- 50 m
    15	- 25 m
    16	
    17	Users can also choose when the mode should disable itself:
    18	
    19	- 1 hour
    20	- 4 hours (default)
    21	- 12 hours
    22	- 24 hours
    23	- Never
    24	
    25	The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.
    26	
    27	Users can also choose how frequent background updates are delivered to the server:
    28	
    29	- Immediately (default)
    30	- Every 30 seconds
    31	- Every minute
    32	- Every 5 minutes
    33	- Every 10 minutes
    34	
    35	Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.
    36	
    37	The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and delivery mode. These explanations make the battery and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.
    38	
    39	Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.
    40	
    41	## Runtime Behavior
    42	
    43	`SettingsManager` owns the new persisted settings and normalizes unsupported distance or duration values back to the shipped defaults. The DeviceKey recovery/reset snapshot now includes these settings so that identity changes do not silently reset the user's background-tracking preference.
    44	
    45	`LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.
    46	
    47	When delayed delivery is selected, `LocationManager` passes the selected delay only for non-active app states while frequent background updates are enabled. Foreground updates and the default significant-change mode continue to use immediate delivery.
    48	
    49	`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately.
    50	
    51	The location-status view now shows whether background tracking is using significant-change monitoring or frequent updates. If frequent updates have a finite expiration date, the status card also shows when the mode will revert.
    52	
    53	## Verification
    54	
    55	Validated with:
    56	
    57	```sh
    58	./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh
    59	./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh -only-testing:miataruTests/SettingsConfigurationTests
    60	git diff --check
    61	```
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="apply_patch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **apply_patch**</summary>

```diff
@@
 Users can also choose how frequent background updates are delivered to the server:
 
 - Immediately (default)
 - Every 30 seconds
 - Every minute
 - Every 5 minutes
 - Every 10 minutes
 
 Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.
 
-The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, and delivery mode. These explanations make the battery and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.
+When frequent background updates are enabled, users can also choose how often Miataru checks visitor history after successful background uploads:
+
+- Every update
+- Every minute
+- Every 5 minutes
+- Every 10 minutes (default)
+- Every 30 minutes
+- Every hour
+
+This affects the Unknown Visitor Alerts follow-up request only. Location uploads continue to use the selected server-delivery behavior. The 10-minute default reduces repeated `GetVisitorHistory` requests while preserving the old "every update" behavior as an explicit option.
+
+The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, delivery mode, and visitor-check interval. These explanations make the battery, network, and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.
@@
 `LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.
 
 When delayed delivery is selected, `LocationManager` passes the selected delay only for non-active app states while frequent background updates are enabled. Foreground updates and the default significant-change mode continue to use immediate delivery.
 
-`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately.
+For frequent background uploads, `LocationManager` also passes the selected visitor-check minimum interval into the delivery path. Immediate successful sends call `UnknownVisitorAlertService` with that interval; queued sends persist the interval on the outbox item so a later flush still applies the same throttling decision.
+
+`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately. When a queued item is delivered, its stored visitor-check interval is forwarded to the unknown-visitor alert processing path.
+
+`UnknownVisitorAlertService` stores the last background visitor-check attempt timestamp. If the next successful frequent-background upload arrives before the configured interval has elapsed, the visitor-history request is skipped. Foreground uploads and the unchanged significant-change background default do not pass an interval and therefore keep the previous behavior.
```

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-26 09:12:39Z)**_

Erledigt. Der frequent-background-Modus hat jetzt eine zusätzliche Einstellung “Besucher prüfen” mit Optionen: jedes Update, 1 min, 5 min, 10 min default, 30 min, 60 min. Das alte Verhalten bleibt als “jedes Update” wählbar, aber ohne Nutzerkonfiguration gilt jetzt im aktivierten Hintergrundmodus 10 Minuten.

Die Logik ist so verdrahtet, dass nur frequent-background Updates im Hintergrund das Intervall an `UnknownVisitorAlertService` weitergeben. Foreground und der normale Significant-Change-Default bleiben unverändert. Queued/delayed Updates speichern das Intervall im Outbox-Item, damit ein späterer Flush dieselbe Drosselung nutzt.

Ich sehe: lokale Notifications sind schon zentral im AppDelegate verdrahtet, aber es gibt noch keinen Tap-Handler und keinen internen “öffne diese Settings-Unterseite”-Mechanismus. Ich baue deshalb einen kleinen App-Navigationskoordinator plus einen testbaren Reminder-Service, statt die Notification-Logik direkt in Views zu verstecken.

     1	version 3.1.7
     2	- Added an opt-in frequent background location-update mode in Advanced Options, keeping significant-change monitoring as the unchanged default when the user does not enable it.
     3	- Added configurable frequent-background distance presets (100 m default, 50 m, 25 m) and auto-disable durations (1 hour, 4 hours default, 12 hours, 24 hours, never), with automatic fallback to significant-change monitoring after expiry.
     4	- Added frequent-background delivery options so updates can keep sending immediately by default or be queued locally and flushed together after 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, or 10 minutes.
     5	- Added configurable visitor-history check intervals for frequent background mode, defaulting to 10 minutes so visitor checks no longer have to run after every background location upload.
     6	- Added localized per-option explanations for frequent background movement threshold, auto-disable duration, server-delivery mode, and visitor-check interval choices.
     7	- Added localized red battery-usage warning text while frequent background updates are enabled, plus background-mode/expiry visibility in the location-status view.
     8	- Preserved frequent-background update settings during DeviceKey recovery/reset flows and added regression coverage for defaults, localization parity, value normalization, expiry behavior, and default significant-change configuration.
     9	- Incremented iOS app build number (`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`) from 1 to 2.
    10	- Fixed offline `UpdateLocation` delivery so new updates are queued behind already pending outbox items and retried in FIFO order without replacing the original event payload metadata.
    11	- Added a location-status statistic for queued location updates that still need to be sent.
    12	- Added Advanced Options controls for the unsent location-update queue retention and capacity, keeping the default at 24 hours / 500 updates while allowing longer retention, unlimited retention, and higher caps.
    13	- Added a confirmation step when changing the Miataru server URL while location updates are queued, allowing the user to send queued updates to the new server or discard them.
    14	- Improved queued-update draining so active tracking schedules near-term FIFO flushes, full batches continue automatically, and the location-status view can manually flush all currently deliverable queued updates.
    15	- Hardened queued-update server URL retargeting so already queued items are consistently rewritten to the chosen new server and in-flight old-URL sends cannot remove retargeted queue records.
    16	- Added regression coverage for queued-update ordering, configurable outbox policy changes, server URL retargeting, full queue flushes, and settings/localization parity.
    17	- Added visible loading feedback when opening a device's location history on iPhone and iPad, including the selected device name/ID while history data is being preloaded.
    18	- Prevented the history map from briefly showing the "no location history" fallback before cached or freshly loaded history entries have been applied.
    19	- Improved history-load error handling so invalid configuration, server/response failures, encoding/decoding failures, network failures, and unknown failures produce readable user-facing messages.
    20	- Added full localization coverage for the new history loading text across all supported app languages.
    21	- Made common error overlays wrap long messages more reliably and kept history preload errors visible longer.
    22	- Kept manual pan/zoom interaction on the device history map authoritative during live history refreshes, so newly recorded positions no longer force the map to refit after the user has adjusted the camera.
    23	
    24	version 3.1.5
    25	- Refactored the iOS settings flow: centralized runtime defaults and one-time existing-install migrations, shortened the root settings screen, added a dedicated `Advanced Options` page, and moved ACL/status content to the intended destinations.
    26	- Synchronized settings defaults, labels, picker options, and explanatory copy across `Localizable.xcstrings` and all supported `Settings.bundle` locales.
    27	- Added regression coverage for settings defaults, settings localization completeness, `Settings.bundle` parity, and the advanced-options navigation path, with updated test documentation.
    28	- Fixed device-slogan editing so normal spaces remain typeable while final save cleansing still trims outer whitespace and removes control characters.
    29	- Changed the device-slogan fetch strategy: `Add Device` and `Edit Device` use `getDeviceSlogan`, unknown devices in the iPhone/iPad device lists only fetch missing slogans individually after the normal `getLocation` refresh, and all other slogan reads continue to rely on `getLocation`.

     1	# Frequent Background Location Updates
     2	
     3	## Problem
     4	
     5	Miataru previously used iOS significant-change monitoring for background location tracking. That behavior is battery-friendly and remains the default, but it only wakes the app after larger movement. Some users need a temporary mode that reports background movement more often without changing the default behavior for everyone else.
     6	
     7	## Change
     8	
     9	Advanced Options now include an explicit frequent-background update toggle in the background location section. The toggle defaults to off, so existing users continue to use significant-change monitoring unless they opt in.
    10	
    11	When the mode is enabled, users can choose a background distance filter:
    12	
    13	- 100 m (default)
    14	- 50 m
    15	- 25 m
    16	
    17	Users can also choose when the mode should disable itself:
    18	
    19	- 1 hour
    20	- 4 hours (default)
    21	- 12 hours
    22	- 24 hours
    23	- Never
    24	
    25	The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.
    26	
    27	Users can also choose how frequent background updates are delivered to the server:
    28	
    29	- Immediately (default)
    30	- Every 30 seconds
    31	- Every minute
    32	- Every 5 minutes
    33	- Every 10 minutes
    34	
    35	Delayed delivery stores updates in the persistent local outbox first. The first delayed update starts a delivery window; additional updates that arrive before that window closes share the same release time. When the window is reached, the queued updates are flushed together through the existing FIFO delivery path.
    36	
    37	When frequent background updates are enabled, users can also choose how often Miataru checks visitor history after successful background uploads:
    38	
    39	- Every update
    40	- Every minute
    41	- Every 5 minutes
    42	- Every 10 minutes (default)
    43	- Every 30 minutes
    44	- Every hour
    45	
    46	This affects the Unknown Visitor Alerts follow-up request only. Location uploads continue to use the selected server-delivery behavior. The 10-minute default reduces repeated `GetVisitorHistory` requests while preserving the old "every update" behavior as an explicit option.
    47	
    48	The in-app Advanced Options screen shows a localized explanation for the currently selected movement threshold, auto-disable duration, delivery mode, and visitor-check interval. These explanations make the battery, network, and behavior tradeoffs visible without requiring an extra alert.
    49	
    50	Because this mode uses regular background location updates instead of significant-change monitoring, the settings view shows a localized red warning while the option is enabled to explain the expected higher battery usage.
    51	
    52	## Runtime Behavior
    53	
    54	`SettingsManager` owns the new persisted settings and normalizes unsupported distance or duration values back to the shipped defaults. The DeviceKey recovery/reset snapshot now includes these settings so that identity changes do not silently reset the user's background-tracking preference.
    55	
    56	`LocationManager` keeps the existing significant-change path as the default. Only when the frequent mode is enabled and not expired does it start regular background location updates with the selected `distanceFilter`. Expiration is checked on startup, app foreground/background transitions, tracking-mode updates, setting changes, timer expiry, and incoming background location updates.
    57	
    58	When delayed delivery is selected, `LocationManager` passes the selected delay only for non-active app states while frequent background updates are enabled. Foreground updates and the default significant-change mode continue to use immediate delivery.
    59	
    60	For frequent background uploads, `LocationManager` also passes the selected visitor-check minimum interval into the delivery path. Immediate successful sends call `UnknownVisitorAlertService` with that interval; queued sends persist the interval on the outbox item so a later flush still applies the same throttling decision.
    61	
    62	`LocationUpdateDeliveryCoordinator` stores delayed updates with an `availableAfter` timestamp. Periodic, network-recovery, and app-activation flushes respect that timestamp, while explicit manual/server-change flushes can drain the queue immediately. When a queued item is delivered, its stored visitor-check interval is forwarded to the unknown-visitor alert processing path.
    63

+import Combine
+import Foundation
+
+enum AppRootNavigationDestination {
+    case settings
+}
+
+enum SettingsNavigationDestination {
+    case advancedOptions
+}
+
+struct SettingsNavigationRequest: Equatable, Identifiable {
+    let id = UUID()
+    let destination: SettingsNavigationDestination
+}
+
+@MainActor
+final class AppNavigationCoordinator: ObservableObject {
+    static let shared = AppNavigationCoordinator()
+
+    @Published private(set) var rootDestination: AppRootNavigationDestination?
+    @Published private(set) var settingsRequest: SettingsNavigationRequest?
+
+    private init() {}
+
+    func openAdvancedSettings() {
+        rootDestination = .settings
+        settingsRequest = SettingsNavigationRequest(destination: .advancedOptions)
+    }
+
+    func consumeSettingsRequest(_ request: SettingsNavigationRequest) {
+        guard settingsRequest?.id == request.id else { return }
+        settingsRequest = nil
+        rootDestination = nil
+    }
+}

```diff
+/*
+ * Copyright (c) 2013-2026, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com
+ *
+ * FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService.swift
+ * miataru
+ *
+ * Created by Codex on 26.04.26.
+ */
+
+import Foundation
+import UserNotifications
+
+protocol FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying {
+    func authorizationStatus() async -> UNAuthorizationStatus
+    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool
+    func pendingNotificationRequests() async -> [UNNotificationRequest]
+    func add(_ request: UNNotificationRequest) async throws
+    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async
+    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async
+}
+
+struct LiveFrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifier: FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying {
+    func authorizationStatus() async -> UNAuthorizationStatus {
+        await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
+            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getNotificationSettings { settings in
+                continuation.resume(returning: settings.authorizationStatus)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool {
+        try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
+            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: options) { granted, error in
+                if let error {
+                    continuation.resume(throwing: error)
+                } else {
+                    continuation.resume(returning: granted)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    func pendingNotificationRequests() async -> [UNNotificationRequest] {
+        await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
+            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getPendingNotificationRequests { requests in
+                continuation.resume(returning: requests)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    func add(_ request: UNNotificationRequest) async throws {
+        try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>) in
+            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) { error in
+                if let error {
+                    continuation.resume(throwing: error)
+                } else {
+                    continuation.resume(returning: ())
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
+        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers: identifiers)
+    }
+
+    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
+        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers: identifiers)
+    }
+}
+
+actor FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService {
+    static let shared = FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService()
+
+    static let notificationIdentifier = "frequent_background_tracking_reminder"
+    static let notificationType = "frequent_background_tracking_reminder"
+    static let notificationTypeUserInfoKey = UnknownVisitorAlertService.notificationTypeUserInfoKey
+    static let reminderInterval: TimeInterval = 24 * 60 * 60
+
+    private let notifier: FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying
+
+    init(notifier: FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying = LiveFrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifier()) {
+        self.notifier = notifier
+    }
+
+    func refresh(locationTrackingEnabled: Bool,
+                 frequentBackgroundUpdatesEnabled: Bool,
+                 durationMode: FrequentBackgroundLocationUpdateDuration) async {
+        guard locationTrackingEnabled,
+              frequentBackgroundUpdatesEnabled,
+              durationMode == .unlimited else {
+            await cancel()
+            return
+        }
+
+        await scheduleIfNeeded()
+    }
+
+    func cancel() async {
+        await notifier.removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers: [Self.notificationIdentifier])
+        await notifier.removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers: [Self.notificationIdentifier])
+    }
+
+    private func scheduleIfNeeded() async {
+        guard await ensureAuthorization() else {
+            await cancel()
+            return
+        }
+
+        let pendingRequests = await notifier.pendingNotificationRequests()
+        if pendingRequests.contains(where: { $0.identifier == Self.notificationIdentifier }) {
+            return
+        }
+
+        let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()
+        content.title = NSLocalizedString(
+            "frequent_background_location_reminder_notification_title",
+            comment: "Notification title reminding the user that never-expiring frequent background tracking is still active"
+        )
+        content.body = NSLocalizedString(
+            "frequent_background_location_reminder_notification_body",
+            comment: "Notification body explaining that tapping opens Advanced Options to disable frequent background tracking"
+        )
+        content.sound = .default
+        content.userInfo = [
+            Self.notificationTypeUserInfoKey: Self.notificationType
+        ]
+
+        let trigger = UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger(
+            timeInterval: Self.reminderInterval,
+            repeats: true
+        )
+        let request = UNNotificationRequest(
+            identifier: Self.notificationIdentifier,
+            content: content,
+            trigger: trigger
+        )
+
+        do {
+            try await notifier.add(request)
+        } catch {
+            debugLog("[FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService] Failed scheduling reminder notification: \(error)")
+        }
+    }
+
+    private func ensureAuthorization() async -> Bool {
+        let status = await notifier.authorizationStatus()
+        switch status {
+        case .authorized, .provisional, .ephemeral:
+            return true
+        case .notDetermined:
+            do {
+                return try await notifier.requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound])
+            } catch {
+                debugLog("[FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService] Notification authorization request failed: \(error)")
+                return false
+            }
+        case .denied:
+            return false
+        @unknown default:
+            return false
+        }
+    }
+}

+    private let requestAuthorizationResult: Result<Bool, Error>
+    private(set) var didRequestAuthorization: Bool = false
+    private(set) var pendingRequests: [UNNotificationRequest]
+    private(set) var addedRequests: [UNNotificationRequest] = []
+    private(set) var removedPendingIdentifiers: [String] = []
+    private(set) var removedDeliveredIdentifiers: [String] = []
+
+    init(initialStatus: UNAuthorizationStatus,
+         pendingRequests: [UNNotificationRequest] = [],
+         requestAuthorizationResult: Result<Bool, Error> = .success(false)) {
+        self.status = initialStatus
+        self.pendingRequests = pendingRequests
+        self.requestAuthorizationResult = requestAuthorizationResult
+    }
+

+    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool {

+        switch requestAuthorizationResult {

+            return granted
+        case .failure(let error):
+            throw error
+        }
+    }

+    }

+        pendingRequests.removeAll { $0.identifier == request.identifier }
+        pendingRequests.append(request)
+    }
+
+    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
+        removedPendingIdentifiers.append(contentsOf: identifiers)
+        pendingRequests.removeAll { identifiers.contains($0.identifier) }
+    }

+    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {

```diff
@@
 The expiration is stored as a date when the option is enabled or when the duration changes. Once the date has passed, the app disables the frequent mode and returns to significant-change monitoring automatically. The "Never" option stores no expiration date.
+
+When the mode is enabled with "Never", Miataru schedules a repeating local reminder notification every 24 hours while normal location tracking is also enabled. The reminder is not rescheduled on every app launch or setting refresh, so the 24-hour timer is not accidentally pushed out forever. If the user turns location tracking off, disables frequent background updates, or changes the duration back to a finite value, the pending reminder and any delivered reminder are removed.
@@
 `UnknownVisitorAlertService` stores the last background visitor-check attempt timestamp. If the next successful frequent-background upload arrives before the configured interval has elapsed, the visitor-history request is skipped. Foreground uploads and the unchanged significant-change background default do not pass an interval and therefore keep the previous behavior.
 
+`FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService` owns the 24-hour repeating local notification for the "Never" duration. It requests alert/sound notification permission only when the active combination requires the reminder, keeps an existing pending reminder instead of resetting its trigger, and cancels the reminder whenever the active combination is no longer true. The notification carries a Miataru notification-type marker so the app delegate can distinguish it from unknown-visitor alerts.
+
+`AppNavigationCoordinator` handles the reminder tap. The app delegate routes the tap to the Settings tab, and the settings view opens Advanced Options programmatically so the frequent-background toggle is visible and can be disabled.
+
 The location-status view now shows whether background tracking is using significant-change monitoring or frequent updates. If frequent updates have a finite expiration date, the status card also shows when the mode will revert.
```
</details></tool-use>

falls bisher keine notifications erlaubt sind wird das dann auch geprüft wenn der neue modus aktiviert wird?


_**User (2026-04-27 00:02:39Z)**_

falls bisher keine notifications erlaubt sind wird das dann auch geprüft wenn der neue modus aktiviert wird?


---

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-27 00:02:55Z)**_

Ja, aber nur für den relevanten Fall: wenn der Frequent-Background-Modus aktiv ist **und** die Dauer auf **„Nie“** steht.

Dann macht `FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService` beim Refresh:

- `authorized/provisional/ephemeral`: Reminder wird geplant.
- `notDetermined`: iOS Notification-Permission wird angefragt.
- `denied`: es wird nichts geplant, weil iOS keine zweite System-Abfrage erlaubt; der Nutzer müsste Notifications in den iOS-App-Einstellungen aktivieren.

Der Check läuft beim Ändern der Settings, beim App-Start sowie bei Foreground/Background-Übergängen. Was aktuell noch fehlt: ein sichtbarer Hinweis in der UI, falls Notifications bereits verweigert wurden und deshalb die 24h-Erinnerung nicht zugestellt werden kann.

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-27 00:05:52Z)**_

Ich werde das als Teil desselben Notification-Services lösen: finite Laufzeiten bekommen eine einmalige “Standardmodus wieder aktiv”-Notification zum Ablaufzeitpunkt, und falls die App den Ablauf selbst verarbeitet, wird zusätzlich sichergestellt, dass diese Notification nicht verloren geht. So ist es robuster als nur ein In-App-Timer.

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-27 00:06:51Z)**_

Ich habe zwei Dinge im Blick: keine falsche Notification bei manuellem Ausschalten, aber auch keine verlorene Notification, wenn die Automatik genau zum Ablaufzeitpunkt den Pending-Reminder entfernt. Dafür speichere ich den geplanten Ablaufzeitpunkt im Notification-Service und entferne die Ablauf-Notification nur, solange sie noch wirklich in der Zukunft liegt.

```diff
@@
 When the mode is enabled with "Never", Miataru schedules a repeating local reminder notification every 24 hours while normal location tracking is also enabled. The reminder is not rescheduled on every app launch or setting refresh, so the 24-hour timer is not accidentally pushed out forever. If the user turns location tracking off, disables frequent background updates, or changes the duration back to a finite value, the pending reminder and any delivered reminder are removed.
+
+For finite durations, Miataru also schedules a one-shot local notification at the stored expiration date. That notification tells the user that the temporary frequent-background mode ended and Miataru has returned to the standard background update mode. If the user manually disables the mode before the expiration date, the pending expiration notification is removed. If the automatic expiration is already due, the notification is left in place so the settings refresh that turns the mode off cannot accidentally cancel the user-facing notice.
@@
-`FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService` owns the 24-hour repeating local notification for the "Never" duration. It requests alert/sound notification permission only when the active combination requires the reminder, keeps an existing pending reminder instead of resetting its trigger, and cancels the reminder whenever the active combination is no longer true. The notification carries a Miataru notification-type marker so the app delegate can distinguish it from unknown-visitor alerts.
+`FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService` owns the 24-hour repeating local notification for the "Never" duration and the one-shot expiration notification for finite durations. It requests alert/sound notification permission only when the active combination requires a notification, keeps an existing pending reminder instead of resetting its trigger, and cancels pending notifications whenever they are no longer relevant. The expiration notification stores its target date so manual disables can cancel future notifications while automatic expiry cannot swallow a notification that is already due. The notifications carry Miataru notification-type markers so the app delegate can distinguish them from unknown-visitor alerts.
 
-`AppNavigationCoordinator` handles the reminder tap. The app delegate routes the tap to the Settings tab, and the settings view opens Advanced Options programmatically so the frequent-background toggle is visible and can be disabled.
+`AppNavigationCoordinator` handles reminder and expiration notification taps. The app delegate routes the tap to the Settings tab, and the settings view opens Advanced Options programmatically so the frequent-background setting is visible.
```
</details></tool-use>

import Foundation
import UserNotifications

protocol FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying {
    func authorizationStatus() async -> UNAuthorizationStatus
    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool
    func pendingNotificationRequests() async -> [UNNotificationRequest]
    func add(_ request: UNNotificationRequest) async throws
    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async
    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async
}

struct LiveFrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifier: FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderNotifying {
    func authorizationStatus() async -> UNAuthorizationStatus {
        await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getNotificationSettings { settings in
                continuation.resume(returning: settings.authorizationStatus)
            }
        }
    }

    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool {
        try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: options) { granted, error in
                if let error {
                    continuation.resume(throwing: error)
                } else {
                    continuation.resume(returning: granted)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    func pendingNotificationRequests() async -> [UNNotificationRequest] {
        await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getPendingNotificationRequests { requests in
                continuation.resume(returning: requests)
            }
        }
    }

    func add(_ request: UNNotificationRequest) async throws {
        try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>) in
            UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) { error in
                if let error {
                    continuation.resume(throwing: error)
                } else {
                    continuation.resume(returning: ())
                }
            }
        }
    }

    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers: identifiers)
    }

    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers: identifiers)
    }
}

    static let shared = FrequentBackgroundTrackingReminderService()

        self.notifier = notifier
        self.nowProvider = nowProvider
    }

    func refresh(locationTrackingEnabled: Bool,
                 frequentBackgroundUpdatesEnabled: Bool,
                 durationMode: FrequentBackgroundLocationUpdateDuration,

        }

    func requestAuthorization(options: UNAuthorizationOptions) async throws -> Bool {
        _ = options
        didRequestAuthorization = true
        switch requestAuthorizationResult {
        case .success(let granted):

            return granted

    func pendingNotificationRequests() async -> [UNNotificationRequest] {
        pendingRequests

    func add(_ request: UNNotificationRequest) async throws {
        addedRequests.append(request)
        pendingRequests.removeAll { $0.identifier == request.identifier }
        pendingRequests.append(request)
    }

    func removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
        removedPendingIdentifiers.append(contentsOf: identifiers)
        pendingRequests.removeAll { identifiers.contains($0.identifier) }
    }

    func removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers identifiers: [String]) async {
        removedDeliveredIdentifiers.append(contentsOf: identifiers)

    @discardableResult
    private func handleFrequentBackgroundLocationExpirationIfNeeded(now: Date = Date()) -> Bool {
        let didExpire = settings.disableExpiredFrequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesIfNeeded(now: now)
        if didExpire {
            debugLog("[LocationManager] Frequent background updates expired; returning to significant-change monitoring")
        } else {
            settings.ensureFrequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesExpiration(now: now)
        }
        scheduleFrequentBackgroundLocationExpirationTimer()
        return didExpire
    }

    private func scheduleFrequentBackgroundLocationExpirationTimer() {
        frequentBackgroundLocationExpirationTimer?.invalidate()
        frequentBackgroundLocationExpirationTimer = nil

        guard settings.frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesEnabled,
              let expiresAt = settings.frequentBackgroundLocationUpdatesExpiresAt else {
            return
        }

        let interval = expiresAt.timeIntervalSinceNow
        guard interval > 0 else { return }

        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: interval, repeats: false) { [weak self] _ in
            guard let self else { return }
            if self.handleFrequentBackgroundLocationExpirationIfNeeded(), self.isTracking {
                self.updateTrackingMode()
            }
        }
        frequentBackgroundLocationExpirationTimer = timer
        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
    }

    static func backgroundUpdateConfiguration(frequentUpdatesEnabled: Bool,
                                              distanceFilterMeters: Int) -> BackgroundUpdateConfiguration {
        guard frequentUpdatesEnabled else {
            return BackgroundUpdateConfiguration(
                usesSignificantChangeMonitoring: true,
                distanceFilter: kCLDistanceFilterNone,
                desiredAccuracy: kCLLocationAccuracyHundredMeters
            )
        }

        let normalizedDistance = FrequentBackgroundLocationDistanceFilter.normalized(distanceFilterMeters)
        return BackgroundUpdateConfiguration(
            usesSignificantChangeMonitoring: false,
            distanceFilter: CLLocationDistance(normalizedDistance),
            desiredAccuracy: backgroundDesiredAccuracy(for: normalizedDistance)
        )
    }

    private static func backgroundDesiredAccuracy(for distanceFilterMeters: Int) -> CLLocationAccuracy {
        distanceFilterMeters <= 50 ? kCLLocationAccuracyNearestTenMeters : kCLLocationAccuracyHundredMeters
    }
    
    // MARK: - Permissions
    func requestLocationPermission() {
        switch locationManager.authorizationStatus {
        case .notDetermined:
            locationManager.requestWhenInUseAuthorization()
        case .authorizedWhenInUse:
            locationManager.requestAlwaysAuthorization()
        case .authorizedAlways:
            // Permission already granted, no action needed
            break
        case .denied, .restricted:
            // Permission was denied, open Settings so user can change it
            openAppSettings()
        @unknown default:
            break
        }
    }

        let url = repoRootURL().appendingPathComponent("miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/Settings.bundle/\(locale).lproj/Root.strings")

    private func loadSettingsBundleSpecifiers() throws -> [[String: Any]] {
        let url = repoRootURL().appendingPathComponent("miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/Settings.bundle/Root.plist")
        let data = try Data(contentsOf: url)
        let plist = try #require(PropertyListSerialization.propertyList(from: data, format: nil) as? [String: Any])
        return try #require(plist["PreferenceSpecifiers"] as? [[String: Any]])
    }

    private func repoRootURL() -> URL {
        let testFileURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: #filePath)

+When the mode is enabled with "Never", Miataru schedules a repeating local reminder notification every 24 hours while normal location tracking is also enabled. The reminder is not rescheduled on every app launch or setting refresh, so the 24-hour timer is not accidentally pushed out forever. If the user turns location tracking off, disables frequent background updates, or changes the duration back to a finite value, the pending reminder and any delivered reminder are removed.
+
+For finite durations, Miataru also schedules a one-shot local notification at the stored expiration date. That notification tells the user that the temporary frequent-background mode ended and Miataru has returned to the standard background update mode. If the user manually disables the mode before the expiration date, the pending expiration notification is removed. If the automatic expiration is already due, the notification is left in place so the settings refresh that turns the mode off cannot accidentally cancel the user-facing notice.
